title: Saṅkalpa for the upasthāna (midday)

samasa.meaning: the worship of the Sun standing near

translation.literal: The upasthāna of Āditya I shall perform.
translation.readable: I shall now stand in worship before the Sun.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, before the midday upasthāna. The witness prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, ‘by way of destroying all the faults I have incurred, for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord’) once, and then only this closing part for each time of day; the opening is said before it. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.
in_the_rite: Midday service, step gayatri-upasthana (M gives it as the midday form of this saṅkalpa).

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.
